title: Cellular-resolution optogenetics reveals attenuation-by-suppression in visual cortical neurons
goal: Reproduce cellular optogenetic response attenuation relative to visual stimulation and cell-level response variability using the original empirical conditions and source-defined analysis populations. Preserve the visual-state and optogenetic-power comparisons, stimulus-response subtraction and windows, and the fluorescence-adjusted variability and measurement-noise controls needed for these named findings.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: The retained cellular attenuation/visual-stimulation comparison and response heterogeneity findings, with Figures 2–3 visual-state and power comparisons and Figure 5/S13 variability controls insofar as they support those named findings. Preserve source-defined analysis populations, response subtraction/windows and fluorescence adjustment. This is not an every-figure, acquisition or raw-movie requirement.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: Figure 4/S11–S12 IO-curve estimation and comparison of the source function families as a separate empirical modeling result. Its fit criterion is not equivalent to reproduction or improvement of the primary attenuation and heterogeneity findings.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
Use an explicitly bound reproduction proposal only within its declared eligibility, comparison and execution limits; copying published findings is insufficient.

The preserved improvement.v1.json retains its declared comparison and coverage. Use retained_secondary_scope for its relationship to the corrected primary findings; satisfying a secondary or partial-component criterion alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement.

The primary same-target outcome bundle is unavailable. Any primary improvement requires an independently justified source-grounded comparison; no replacement metric, direction or tolerance is invented.
Keep the paper+data and paper+data+author-code outcomes separate. All scientific outcomes remain unknown until qualifying original-data execution and independent verification.
Preserve prior task definitions, improvement criteria and useful secondary implementations with their original scopes. Historical attempts and source metadata do not become qualified AI results.
